info.title: Monid Finance API
info.summary: A Financial Datasets-compatible finance REST API backed by Monid providers.
info.description:
US equities fundamentals, prices, filings, news, insider trades, and a stock screener, generated faithfully from this repository's Go source (go/httpapi/rest.go, go/service, go/fd). This server is drop-in compatible with the Financial Datasets REST and MCP interface: the same route shapes, the same query parameters, and response objects whose field names and field order match the Financial Datasets contract (docs/fd-contract-reference.json). It is an independent, Monid-backed implementation; it is not affiliated with or endorsed by Financial Datasets, and no Financial Datasets data or outputs are used.

**Bring your own Monid API key.** Every request carries the caller's own key in the `X-API-KEY` header. Usage bills that caller's own Monid wallet; this server never stores or logs the key. Get a key at https://monid.ai.

**Not every documented route is implemented.** Fifteen routes call live Monid providers; twenty more are registered for Financial Datasets route parity and always answer a zero-cost `{"error": "not_implemented", ...}` (tag: Not implemented). See docs/compatibility.md for the phased plan and docs/openapi-notes.md for how this document was derived.

**Errors and soft failures.** Every failure — real HTTP error and zero-cost soft failure alike — uses the two-key body `{"error": <code>, "message": <detail>}`. Some routes answer `not_found` with HTTP 200 rather than a 4xx status (see each operation's description).

**Pagination.** List routes return a wrapped envelope (e.g. `{"income_statements": [...], "next_page_url": "..."}`) with opaque, server-minted base64url `cursor` tokens. Pages hold 10 records (100 for /prices). `next_page_url` is an absolute URL on this deployment's own host, present only when more records remain.

get.description:
Fetches a company's income statement history: revenue, expenses, and net income over annual, quarterly, or trailing-twelve-month (ttm) reporting periods. Sourced from Monid's DefiLlama `/equities/v1/statements` endpoint, joined against `/equities/v1/filings` for SEC identity (accession number, form type, filing URL/date). ttm rows are derived locally from the four most recent quarters and omit fiscal_period, currency, and filing identity.

period default note: the underlying get_income_statement MCP tool's own JSON Schema default is "ttm" (docs/fd-mcp-tool-schemas.json), matching Financial Datasets. This REST route always fills a period value before calling that tool, so an omitted `period` query parameter defaults to "annual" here instead. Pass `period=ttm` explicitly for trailing-twelve-month rows.

parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens).

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting period. REST-level default is "annual" (see description); the tool/FD-schema default is "ttm".

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of records to retrieve (default: 4, max: 100).

parameters.name: as_reported
parameters.description: Accepted for FD parameter parity but always rejected: as_reported=true answers 400 bad_request ("as_reported is not supported; use the normalized income-statements endpoint") at zero cost.

parameters.name: report_period
parameters.description: Exact report_period date filter (YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.description: report_period >= this date (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive).

parameters.name: report_period_lte
parameters.description: report_period <= this date (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive).

parameters.description: report_period > this date (YYYY-MM-DD, exclusive).

parameters.description: report_period < this date (YYYY-MM-DD, exclusive).

parameters.description: Opaque base64url pagination cursor from a previous response's next_page_url. Omit for the first page.

200.description: A page of income statements, newest report_period first. Real AAPL FY2025/FY2024 10-K values (docs/fd-live-samples/income_statements.json).

get.description:
Fetches a company's balance sheet history: assets, liabilities, and shareholders' equity at each period end. Sourced and joined the same way as /financials/income-statements. ttm balance rows are point-in-time (carried from the latest quarter, not summed) and omit fiscal_period, currency, and filing identity.

period default note: the underlying get_balance_sheet MCP tool's own JSON Schema default is "ttm", matching Financial Datasets. This REST route always fills a period value before calling that tool, so an omitted `period` query parameter defaults to "annual" here instead.

get.description:
Fetches historical financial-metrics rows (margins, turnovers, growth rates, per-share figures) computed from the statement matrix, one row per reporting period. Valuation fields that need a historical market price (enterprise_value, price_to_* ratios, EV multiples, free_cash_flow_yield, peg_ratio, return_on_invested_capital) plus currency and filing_datetime are never sourced and are always omitted; margins/ROE/ROA use ending balances, turnovers use average balances. ttm rows also omit accession_number, form_type, filing_url, and filing_date.

period default note: the underlying get_financial_metrics MCP tool's own JSON Schema default is "ttm". This REST route always fills a period value before calling that tool, so an omitted `period` query parameter defaults to "annual" here instead.

get.description: Fetches a snapshot of current financial metrics (market cap, valuation ratios, margins, growth, and per-share figures) from Monid's DefiLlama `/equities/v1/summary` endpoint. Unlike /financial-metrics, this snapshot has a live market price, so valuation fields are populated.

parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens).

get.description:
Returns a flat list of EarningsRecord entries composed from SEC filing events (8-K/10-Q/10-K/20-F).

- Pass `ticker` for that company's most recent SEC filings. The same report_period can appear twice when an 8-K announcement and the matching 10-Q have both been filed (the 8-K sorts first).
- Omit `ticker` for the real-time earnings feed: the most recently filed earnings across covered companies (sourced from the Nasdaq earnings calendar), deduped by ticker.

Known REST quirk: this route accepts a `limit` query parameter for Financial Datasets parameter parity, but the underlying get_earnings tool ignores it — the FD JSON Schema for this tool exposes no limit parameter at all, and the server always returns up to 5 records regardless of the value passed here.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens). Omit for the real-time earnings feed across all covered companies.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Accepted for FD parameter parity but not applied by the underlying tool (see description); the response always holds up to 5 records.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque base64url pagination cursor from a previous response's next_page_url. Omit for the first page.

200.description: Real AAPL 8-K earnings record (docs/fd-live-samples/earnings.json), ticker mode.

get.description:
Lists SEC filings for a ticker, sourced from Monid's DefiLlama `/equities/v1/filings` endpoint. `cik` is accepted for Financial Datasets parameter parity but always answers 400 bad_request ("cik lookup is not supported; pass ticker instead"); only ticker lookup is routed.

`filing_type` may be repeated (`?filing_type=10-K&filing_type=10-Q`) and is validated against 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, 6-K — a stricter enum than Financial Datasets' free-text example (e.g. "DEF 14A" is not accepted here).

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens). Either ticker or cik is accepted, but only ticker is actually routed.

parameters.name: cik
parameters.description: Accepted for FD parameter parity but always answers 400 bad_request; pass ticker instead.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of records to retrieve (default: 10, max: 1000). REST-level default is 10; the get_filings tool/FD-schema default is 100.

parameters.name: filing_type
parameters.description: Filter by filing type(s). Repeat the parameter for multiple types. Invalid or empty values answer 400 bad_request.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque base64url pagination cursor from a previous response's next_page_url. Omit for the first page.

get.description:
Fetches historical OHLCV price bars for a ticker over [start_date, end_date], sourced from Monid's DefiLlama `/equities/v1/ohlcv` endpoint (daily bars) and aggregated locally into week/month/year bars when requested. Prices are returned in ascending time order; `time` is each bar's end date in UTC.

Deviation from the FD JSON Schema: `start_date` and `end_date` are both functionally required here (400 bad_request "start_date and end_date are required" if either is missing) — this server does not compute the FD schema's documented defaults ("1 year before end_date" / "today"). `interval` supports day/week/month/year only; the FD schema's second/minute intervals are not implemented and answer 400. `interval_multiplier` must be 1 (multi-bar intervals are not implemented).

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens).

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Bar interval. The FD schema also lists second/minute; both answer 400 bad_request here.

parameters.name: interval_multiplier
parameters.description: Must be 1 (default). Any other value answers 400 bad_request: multi-bar intervals are not implemented.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Functionally required (see description).

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Functionally required (see description).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque base64url pagination cursor from a previous response's next_page_url. Omit for the first page.

get.description: Fetches the most recent price snapshot for a ticker (latest price plus day change), sourced from Monid's DefiLlama `/equities/v1/summary` endpoint.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens).

200.description: Derived from the real AAPL closing/opening prices for 2026-08-28 (docs/fd-live-samples/prices.json): day_change and day_change_percent are computed from that real bar, not fabricated.

get.summary: Get recent news for a ticker
get.description:
Fetches recent news articles entity-matched to a ticker, sourced from Monid's Context.dev `/news/search` endpoint, sorted newest first.

Deviation: the get_news tool's own description (matching Financial Datasets) says ticker can be omitted for broad market news, but the underlying implementation always answers 400 bad_request ("market-wide news is not routed; pass ticker") when ticker is missing. `ticker` is effectively required.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens). Effectively required (see description).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of records to retrieve (default: 5, max: 10).

200.description: Illustrative shape (no captured live sample committed for this route); title/source/url are structural placeholders, not a claim about a real published article.

news.title: Apple shares rise after strong iPhone demand signals

get.description:
Fetches insider trading transactions for a ticker from the SECForm4 provider's search route.

Deviations: capped at 15 rows total (the FD schema documents a 5000-row max; REST defaults to 10, not the tool's own 100 default, because this route always fills a limit value). `form_type` filtering is not exposed: the validated route does not report form types, and passing it via MCP answers 400 bad_request. `transaction_type` filtering exists on the underlying tool but is not exposed as a REST query parameter. `name` is the raw insider relationship text from the source filing, not a normalized name. title, transaction_code, security_title, and shares_owned_before_transaction are never sourced and are always omitted.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter by the raw insider relationship text.

parameters.name: filing_date
parameters.description: Exact filing_date filter.

parameters.name: filing_date_gte
parameters.description: filing_date >= this date.

parameters.name: filing_date_lte
parameters.description: filing_date <= this date.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of records to retrieve (default: 10, max: 15). REST-level default is 10; the validated route caps at 15 regardless of the FD schema's 5000 max.

200.description: Illustrative shape (no captured live sample committed for this route); values are structural placeholders, not a claim about a real reported transaction.

post.summary: Screen stocks by exchange and market cap
post.description: Screens stocks via Monid's Nasdaq `/get_stock_screener` endpoint. Only two filter fields are executable today: exchange (NASDAQ/NYSE/AMEX) and market_cap (mega/large/mid/small/micro/nano), both with operator=eq — a small subset of the full Financial Datasets screener catalog. Use GET /financials/search/screener/filters to discover the exact executable set. `currency` is accepted for FD parameter parity but only "USD" is supported (any other value answers 400). Never paginated: there is no next_page_url; use `limit` to bound the result set.

200.description: Illustrative shape; market_cap/last_sale/net_change/percent_change are structural placeholders in Nasdaq's own string format, not a claim about real current market values.

get.description: Returns the executable screen_stocks filter catalog: field names, supported operators, and allowed values. Lists only the filters this server can actually execute (exchange, market_cap; eq only), not the full Financial Datasets catalog.

200.description: The real, deterministic filter catalog this server returns.

get.description: Fetches company facts for a ticker from the US company catalog. This route currently sources only ticker and name; every other CompanyFacts field (cik, industry, sector, exchange, is_active, location, sec_filings_url, sic_code, sic_industry, sic_sector) is schema-legal but always omitted today. `cik` is accepted for FD parameter parity but always answers 400 bad_request; only ticker lookup is routed. When the ticker has no US catalog record, this answers HTTP 200 with an ErrorResponse body ({"error": "not_found", ...}) rather than a 4xx status, at zero additional cost.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol (1-20 letters/digits/dots/hyphens). Either ticker or cik is accepted, but only ticker is actually routed.

parameters.name: cik
parameters.description: Accepted for FD parameter parity but always answers 400 bad_request; pass ticker instead.

200.description: Company facts, or a not_found soft failure (see description).

value.message: No US company record exists for ticker ZZZZ.

get.description:
Retrieves specific sections (items) from one SEC filing: fetches the filing index, resolves the matching 10-K/10-Q/8-K, scrapes it (Monid Context.dev `/web/scrape/markdown`), and extracts the requested item section(s).

Deviations from the FD JSON Schema: `year` is required here (400 bad_request "year is required" if missing) even though the FD schema, and the underlying get_filing_items tool itself, support omitting `year` to auto-resolve the latest matching filing — that capability exists only via MCP, not REST. `item` accepts a single item code per request here, not the array the FD schema declares. `include_exhibits` is accepted for FD parameter parity but true always answers 400 bad_request: exhibit extraction is not implemented. When no filing matches, this answers HTTP 200 with an ErrorResponse body rather than a 4xx status, at zero additional cost.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Uppercase-normalized ticker symbol.

parameters.name: filing_type
parameters.description: The filing type.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The filing year. Required here (see description).

parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: The fiscal quarter, for 10-Q filings.

parameters.name: accession_number
parameters.description: Select an exact filing by SEC accession number, e.g. for 8-K filings.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: A single item code, e.g. Item-1, Item-1A. The FD schema declares this as an array; only one value is accepted per request here. Omit to return every detected section.

parameters.name: include_exhibits
parameters.description: Accepted for FD parameter parity but true always answers 400 bad_request; exhibits are not sourced.

200.description: Extracted filing sections, or a not_found soft failure (see description).

items.name: Business
items.text: The Company designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services. [truncated - illustrative excerpt only]

value.message: No 10-K filing matches ticker AAPL, year 1999.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-KEY
ApiKeyAuth.description: The caller's own Monid API key (get one at https://monid.ai). Passed straight through to Monid on every call, so usage bills the caller's own wallet — this is never a shared server-side credential, and the server never logs or stores it. Missing, empty, or malformed values answer 401 unauthorized before any paid call is attempted.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Uniform error/soft-failure body: {"error": <code>, "message": <detail>}. Used both for real HTTP error statuses and for 200 OK "not_found"/"not_implemented" soft failures that this API never bills for.

error.description: Machine-readable error code, e.g. bad_request, unauthorized, payment_required, rate_limited, upstream_error, upstream_schema_changed, upstream_timeout, unsupported, invalid_cursor, not_found, not_implemented.

FinancialMetric.title: FinancialMetric
FinancialMetric.description: One historical financial-metrics record. This response is built dynamically in Go (service.orderMetricsRecord) rather than from a fixed struct, but it follows the fixed key order in service.metricsKeyOrder, reproduced here as the property order. Valuation fields that require a historical market price (enterprise_value, price_to_* ratios, EV multiples, free_cash_flow_yield, peg_ratio, return_on_invested_capital) plus currency and filing_datetime are never sourced by the validated route and are always omitted. ttm rows additionally omit accession_number, form_type, filing_url, and filing_date. Every field is a pointer with omitempty in the Go source: unsourced values are omitted from the response, never nulled or fabricated.

enum: This Financial Datasets route is not implemented by the Monid-backed server yet; the call was free and no data was fabricated.

filters.description: 1-2 filter objects. Only field=exchange or field=market_cap with operator=eq are executable; any other field/operator answers 400 bad_request before any paid call.

field.description: Only exchange and market_cap are executable.

value.description: For exchange: NASDAQ, NYSE, or AMEX. For market_cap: mega, large, mid, small, micro, or nano.

BadRequest.description: 400 Bad Request. Validation failed before any paid Monid call was made (bad_request), or the request is well-formed but names a capability this server deliberately rejects (unsupported), e.g. as_reported=true or a non-USD currency.

value.message: ticker must be 1-20 letters, digits, dots, or hyphens
as_reported is not supported by the Monid-backed server; as_reported=True cannot be answered honestly.
cursor is not a valid opaque pagination token

Unauthorized.description: 401 Unauthorized. The X-API-KEY header was missing, empty, or contained control characters, or (if the operator configured an allowlist) the key is not on it. This check runs before any Monid call.

value.message: Missing or invalid API key.

PaymentRequired.description: 402 Payment Required. The caller's own Monid wallet could not cover the call (Monid returned a blocked/insufficient-funds result).

value.message: Monid run blocked: insufficient wallet balance.

TooManyRequests.description: 429 Too Many Requests. Per-API-key token-bucket rate limit exceeded (default 60/min per key; 10/min for keyless demo traffic, where enabled).

value.message: Rate limit exceeded. Retry shortly.

BadGateway.description: 502 Bad Gateway. The upstream Monid provider call failed for a reason other than auth/funds/timeout (upstream_error), or its payload no longer matches the shape this server parses (upstream_schema_changed).

value.message: provider returned HTTP 500
provider payload is not valid JSON

GatewayTimeout.description: 504 Gateway Timeout. The upstream Monid provider call timed out.

value.message: provider request timed out
